# No Mouse Mode — full text for AI assistants

The complete public text of nomousemode.com in one file: the product page, the support page and every guide.
Short version: https://nomousemode.com/llms.txt

## Product page

Source: https://nomousemode.com/  
Mac menu bar app · macOS 14 Sonoma or later · Apple silicon and Intel · $19.99 one-time for 1 Mac · free updates

No Mouse Mode lets you use your Mac without reaching for the mouse or trackpad. Click any button by typing the two letters on it, or just its name. Glide the pointer, drag, scroll and jump across screens with the keys under your fingers.

### Click anything by typing

- **Click labels (⇧⌘Space):** works in any app, even with No Mouse Mode off. Every button, link, tab, menu, menu bar item and Dock icon gets a small label; type it and it's clicked. Hold ⇧ with the last letter to right-click, ⌘ to ⌘-click (new tab), ⌥ to double-click, ⌃ to just move the pointer there. Tab keeps the labels coming back for several clicks. Labels for a window stay the same each time.
- **Type to click (⇧⌘/):** type part of a button's or text's name (case, spaces and accents ignored; initials work) and press Return.
- **Labels in every app (optional):** for apps that don't describe their buttons to macOS, No Mouse Mode can read on-screen text with Apple's on-device text recognition. Needs Screen Recording; nothing is saved or sent.

### Steer the pointer (⇧⌘M turns No Mouse Mode on)

| Action | Key |
|---|---|
| Move the pointer (smooth, eases in) | W A S D |
| Fast / one-point precise | hold Shift / hold Q |
| Click (twice: double-click, three times: triple-click, hold: drag) | Space |
| Right-click | Return |
| Middle click | M |
| Back / forward buttons | [ / ] |
| Scroll (up, down and sideways) | arrow keys |
| Click labels | F |
| Type to click | / |
| Scroll areas | J |
| Jump grid | E |
| Next / previous display | Tab / Shift-Tab |
| Saved spots | 1–9 jump, Shift-1–9 save |
| Jump back | ` |
| Show every key | H |

Every key and shortcut can be changed in Settings. Shortcuts with ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ always reach the app you're using, and clicking into a text box turns No Mouse Mode off so you can type. You can also list apps where it stays off, or hold Right Command or Right Option to use it only while the key is down.

### Scroll areas and the jump grid

- **Scroll areas (⇧⌘J):** numbers every scrollable pane on screen; pick one, then scroll with J/K or the arrows, page with Space, and jump to the top or bottom with T and B.
- **Jump grid (E):** a 3×3 grid labelled Q W E / A S D / Z X C covers the screen and zooms in with each press, so two or three keys reach any point. Works in every app.

### Learn it in two minutes

A guided setup ends with a hands-on try, the Practice window has nine short lessons that tick themselves off, and H shows every key whenever you forget one.

### Private

Keystrokes are never stored or sent. The app only goes online to activate and re-check your license and to check for updates. It needs Accessibility permission (Screen Recording only if you turn on reading on-screen text).

### Price

- 1 Mac: $19.99 · 3 Macs: $49.99 · 5 Macs: $79.99 · 20 Macs: $299.99
- One-time purchase, free updates, no subscription. No free trial: the website has interactive demos that use the same keys.
- Checkout by Dodo Payments (merchant of record). All sales are final.
- Bought version 1? Version 2 is free on the Mac you already use.

## Support page (https://nomousemode.com/support)

Support

Most questions are answered below. If yours isn't, email [adgan.business@gmail.com](mailto:adgan.business@gmail.com?subject=No%20Mouse%20Mode%20support) and include your macOS version (Apple menu → About This Mac) and No Mouse Mode version (in Applications, right-click No Mouse Mode → Get Info).

### Getting started

### How do I set it up?

Drag No Mouse Mode into your Applications folder and open it. A short setup walks you through the one macOS permission it needs, Accessibility (the page updates by itself once it's switched on), asks for your license key, shows you the two ways to use it, then lets you try it for real. You can open the full Practice (nine short lessons) from the menu bar icon any time.

### Nothing happens when I press Cmd+Shift+M

Check that No Mouse Mode is running: you should see its cursor icon in the menu bar. If it is, another app may be using the same shortcut. Open the menu bar icon, choose **Settings…** and record a different toggle shortcut. If the license isn't activated yet, the app asks for your key first.

### It asks for Accessibility or Input Monitoring permission

macOS requires these for any app that moves the cursor from the keyboard. Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility** and switch on No Mouse Mode, then do the same under **Input Monitoring** if it's listed. Then quit and reopen the app. [Here's exactly what the app does with these permissions.](https://nomousemode.com/privacy)

### Permission is switched on but it still doesn't work

Select No Mouse Mode in the Accessibility list, remove it with the **–** button, then add it back with **+** (it's in your Applications folder) and reopen the app. This resets a permission entry that macOS sometimes keeps from an older copy of the app.

### "This app requires a newer version of macOS"

Version 1.0 only ran on the newest macOS. Current versions run on macOS 14 (Sonoma) and newer. Download the latest version from [nomousemode.com/download](https://nomousemode.com/download) and replace the copy in your Applications folder.

### Your license

### Where do I enter my license key?

The setup asks for it the first time you open the app. You can also open the menu bar icon, choose **Settings…** and go to **License**. Paste the key and click **Activate**. Activation needs an internet connection; after that the app works offline.

### Where do I find my license key?

It's shown on the page you land on after checkout, and it's in the email from Dodo Payments (check spam if it isn't in your inbox). Version 1 was sold on Gumroad; those purchases need no key on the Mac you already use. Can't find it? Email us with the address you used to buy.

### Which license do I need?

One license key works on as many Macs as you bought it for: **1 Mac** ($19.99), **3 Macs** ($49.99), **5 Macs** ($79.99) or **20 Macs** ($299.99). Each is a one-time purchase with free updates. Pick the number of Macs you use at the same time; you can always move a license from an old Mac to a new one with **Deactivate**, so a new Mac doesn't need a new license. See [pricing](https://nomousemode.com/#pricing).

### How do I move my license to another Mac?

On the old Mac, open **Settings… → License** and click **Deactivate**. Then activate the same key on the new Mac. If the old Mac is gone or broken, email us and we'll free up the license for you.

### I bought No Mouse Mode before version 2.0

Thank you! It keeps working on the Mac you already use it on, with no key needed, and the update is free. For a new Mac, email [adgan.business@gmail.com](mailto:adgan.business@gmail.com?subject=No%20Mouse%20Mode%201.x%20license) with the email address you bought with.

### Using No Mouse Mode

### What are the keys?

| W A S D | Move the cursor. It speeds up the longer you hold. |
|---|---|
| Shift (hold) | Fast |
| Q (hold) | Precision: slow and pixel-exact |
| Space | Click. Tap twice to double-click, three times to triple-click. Hold and move to drag. |
| Return | Right-click |
| ↑ ↓ | Scroll up and down |
| ← → | Scroll left and right |
| M | Middle click |
| [ ] | Back and forward (a mouse's side buttons) |
| F | Click labels |
| / | Type to click |
| J | Scroll areas |
| E | Jump grid |
| Tab | Next display (Shift+Tab: previous) |
| 1–9 | Jump to a saved spot. Shift and the number saves one. |
| ` | Jump back to where the cursor was before its last jump |
| H | Show every key |

Turn it on and off with Cmd+Shift+M. These work anywhere, even while it's off: **Cmd+Shift+Space** click labels, **Cmd+Shift+/** type to click, **Cmd+Shift+J** scroll areas. Every key and shortcut can be changed in Settings.

### How does the jump grid work?

Press **E**. The screen with the cursor splits into a 3×3 grid labelled Q W E / A S D / Z X C, the same shape as those keys on your keyboard. Press a letter and the cursor jumps to the middle of that cell, then the grid zooms into it; two or three presses reach anywhere. Press **Space** to click there or **Return** to right-click, **Delete** to go back a level, **Tab** to move the grid to your next display, or **Esc** to close it. You can still fine-tune with W A S D afterwards.

### How do click labels work?

Press **Cmd+Shift+Space** (or **F** while No Mouse Mode is on) and every clickable thing in the front window (buttons, links, tabs, menus, checkboxes and fields), the menu bar and the Dock gets a short letter label. Type the letters and it's clicked. Hold a key while typing the last letter for a different click: **Shift** right-clicks, **Command** Command-clicks (a new tab in browsers), **Option** double-clicks and **Control** only moves the cursor there. **Tab** keeps the labels coming back after each click. **Esc** cancels.

Labels work in Mac apps and on web pages that describe their buttons to macOS, which most do. If an app shows few or no labels, turn on **Also read text on the screen** in Settings → Clicking, or use the jump grid or W A S D, which work everywhere.

### How does type to click work?

Press **Cmd+Shift+/** (or **/** while it's on) and start typing what a button or a piece of text says. Case, spaces and accents don't matter, and first letters work too ("nf" finds New Folder). Matches are outlined; **Tab** moves between them and **Return** clicks. Shift+Return right-clicks, Command+Return Command-clicks and Option+Return double-clicks.

### How do scroll areas work?

Press **Cmd+Shift+J** (or **J** while it's on). Each scrollable part of the front window gets a number and the cursor moves into the first one. Pick another with its number or **Tab**. Then hold the arrow keys or **J**/**K** to scroll (Shift for faster), **Space** to page down, Shift+Space to page up, **T** for the top and **B** for the bottom. **Esc** when you're done.

### Labels and type to click find nothing in one app

Some apps (certain games, design canvases, remote desktops and older cross-platform apps) don't tell macOS where their buttons are. Turn on **Also read text on the screen** in Settings → Clicking and allow **Screen Recording** in System Settings → Privacy & Security when asked; you may need to quit and reopen No Mouse Mode afterwards. It reads the words on screen on your Mac and never saves or sends them. Buttons that are only icons still need the jump grid or W A S D.

### Can I use it just while holding a key?

Yes. In Settings, turn on hold-to-use and choose **Right Command** or **Right Option**. Hold that key, use the mouse keys, and let go to switch back. It's off by default, and Cmd+Shift+M still works either way.

### I can't type while it's on

That's expected for the keys it uses: while No Mouse Mode is on they control the mouse. When you click into a text box it switches itself off so you can type (you can turn that off in Settings → General). Press Cmd+Shift+M to switch it off yourself, use hold-to-use so it's only on while you hold a key, or use the anywhere shortcuts, which never need it on.

### Can it stay off in certain apps?

Yes. Add apps in **Settings → Apps**, or choose **Turn Off Automatically in …** from the menu bar icon while you're in the app. It switches itself off whenever one of them is in front and back on when you leave. Turning it on by hand still works.

### I forgot a key

Press **H** while No Mouse Mode is on to see every key at the bottom of the screen, or open **Keyboard Guide** or **Practice** from the menu bar icon.

### Do keyboard shortcuts still work?

Yes. Any shortcut using Command, Control or Option (like Cmd+S, Cmd+W or Ctrl+→) goes straight to your apps, even while No Mouse Mode is on.

### How do I double-click, right-click or drag?

Tap Space twice quickly to double-click (three times to triple-click). Press Return to right-click. To drag, hold Space, move with W A S D, then release Space.

### The cursor is too slow or too fast

Hold **Shift** for a burst of speed or **Q** for slow, precise movement. To change the normal speed, open **Settings…** from the menu bar icon and adjust the speed settings there.

### Can I change the keys?

Yes. Every key and every shortcut can be changed in Settings. Click a field, then press the key you want. **Restore Defaults** puts them all back.

### Does it work with more than one display?

Yes. The cursor moves across all your displays, Tab jumps to the middle of the next one, and the badge and grid appear on the display the cursor is on. Labels appear wherever the front window is. In the jump grid, Tab moves the grid to the next display.

### Updates, login and removal

### How do I update?

Version 2.0 and later update themselves automatically. Updates are free. You can also check by hand: open the menu bar icon and choose **Check for Updates…**. If you're on version 1.x, download the latest version from [nomousemode.com/download](https://nomousemode.com/download), quit No Mouse Mode from its menu bar icon, and drag the new copy into your Applications folder, replacing the old one.

### Can it start when I log in?

Yes. Turn on **Open No Mouse Mode at login** in Settings → General.

### How do I uninstall it?

If you might use your license on another Mac later, first open **Settings… → License** and click **Deactivate**. Then choose **Quit** from the menu bar icon and drag No Mouse Mode from Applications to the Trash. You can also remove it from the Accessibility, Input Monitoring and Screen Recording lists in System Settings.

### Still stuck?

Email [adgan.business@gmail.com](mailto:adgan.business@gmail.com?subject=No%20Mouse%20Mode%20support) with a short description of what's happening, your macOS version and your No Mouse Mode version.

## Guides & comparison pages (full text)

### The best keyboard mouse apps for Mac in 2026

Source: https://nomousemode.com/best-keyboard-mouse-apps-for-mac  
Updated: 2026-10-31 · Author: Ahmed Gagan (maker of No Mouse Mode)

There's no single best mouseless app, because they do different jobs. **Label apps click buttons, search apps click by name, grid and pointer apps reach anywhere, and macOS has free built-ins that are enough for many people.** Here's what each one is for.

> **Short answer:** For one app that clicks by label or by name *and* moves the pointer, drags, scrolls panes and has a grid, we'd pick [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) (we make it, so weigh that). For label clicking alone, Homerow is the polished, maintained choice. For free, Scoot is open source and maintained, and Shortcat is a free-download beta. Mouseless suits people who also use Windows or Linux. If you only need a mouse now and then, the free macOS built-ins (Mouse Keys, Voice Control, Full Keyboard Access) may be all you need.

#### How we picked (and our bias)

This guide is written by the maker of [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/), so it isn't neutral. To keep it useful anyway, every price, version and date below was checked on the app's official site, docs, changelog, GitHub repository or Homebrew listing on October 31, 2026. Where something wasn't published (a price, a minimum macOS), we say so instead of guessing. We sorted by use case rather than crowning one winner, because a label app and a grid app solve different problems.

The four approaches you'll see:

- **Labels:** letters appear on every button; type one to click it.
- **Search to click:** type a button's name; the app finds and clicks it.
- **Grid:** the screen splits into cells you pick by key, to reach any spot.
- **Free pointer:** keys move the cursor like a mouse would.

Labels and search depend on apps describing their buttons to macOS through accessibility. Most Mac apps and websites do, but some (games, design canvases, remote desktops) don't. Grids and free pointers work everywhere.

#### The whole field at a glance

| App | Price (as of Oct 2026) | Approach | Moves pointer | Grid | Maintained | macOS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No Mouse Mode | $19.99 one time (1 Mac); no trial | Labels, type to click, scroll areas | Yes, W A S D | Yes, 3×3 zooming | Yes, 2.0.1 | 14+ |
| Homerow | $49.99 one time; free to try with a reminder every 50 activations | Labels, scroll, search | Not shown on its site | Not shown on its site | Yes, 1.5.3 (Mar 2026) | 13+ |
| Shortcat | Free download; no price on its site | Search to click, labels | Not listed | Not listed | Last update Jul 2025 (v0.12.2 beta) | 13+ |
| Wooshy | Free with "naps", or $3.88/mo / $46.28/yr | Search to click (incl. Dock, menu bar) | No mode documented | Not documented | Yes | 14.6+ (older builds for Ventura, Monterey) |
| Scoot | Free, open source (BSD-3) | Labels, grid, freestyle | Yes | Yes | Yes, v1.3 (Mar 2026) | README: 11 and 12 |
| Mouseless | Not published (lifetime or subscription); 14-day trial | Grid, free mode, labels (beta) | Yes | Yes | Yes, v1.1.0 (Oct 2026) | 12+ (Homebrew) |
| warpd | Free, open source (MIT) | Hints, grid, normal mode | Yes | Yes | No, last commit Jun 2023 | Unknown |
| Vimac | Free, open source (GPL-3.0) | Hints, scroll mode | Not listed | Not listed | No, last commit Dec 2022; now Homerow | Unknown |
| Mouse Keys | Free, built in | Number keys move the pointer | Yes | No | Part of macOS | Built in |
| Voice Control | Free, built in | Spoken numbers, names and grid | By voice | Yes, by voice | Part of macOS | Built in |
| Full Keyboard Access | Free, built in | Tab focus between controls | No | No | Part of macOS | Built in |
| Vimium | Free, open source (MIT) | Link hints in the browser only | No | No | Yes | Chrome, Edge, Firefox |

"Not shown" or "not listed" means we didn't find the feature on the app's own site or docs. It doesn't prove the app lacks it.

#### 1. No Mouse Mode: best all-in-one keyboard mouse

[No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) 2.0 tries to replace the whole mouse, not just the click. **Click labels** (`⇧⌘Space`) put letters on every button, link, tab and menu in the front window, plus the menu bar and the Dock. **Type to click** (`⇧⌘/`) finds a button by part of its name or its initials. **Scroll areas** (`⇧⌘J`) number each scrollable pane. Press `⇧⌘M` and your keys become the mouse: `W` `A` `S` `D` glide the cursor (Shift for fast, Q for one-pixel precise), `Space` clicks or drags, `Return` right-clicks, `M` middle-clicks, and `E` opens a 3×3 grid that reaches anywhere in two or three presses.

For apps that don't describe their buttons to macOS, it can optionally read on-screen text with Apple's on-device text recognition (needs Screen Recording; nothing is saved or sent). A Practice window with nine lessons teaches the keys. The trade-offs: there's no free trial (the site has in-browser demos instead), it's $19.99 one time for 1 Mac ($49.99 for 3), and it needs macOS 14 Sonoma or later on Apple silicon or Intel. Its default label shortcut is the same `⇧⌘Space` that Shortcat uses and Homerow's demos show, but every shortcut can be changed.

#### 2. Homerow: best for polished label clicking

[Homerow](https://www.homerow.app) offers "keyboard shortcuts for every button in macOS": labels on buttons, links and UI elements, plus scrolling and search. It's the successor of Vimac and is actively maintained (1.5.3, March 2026). It's $49.99 one time and covers all your personal Macs, and it's free to try with a reminder every 50 activations. It needs macOS 13 or later. Its site doesn't show a free-pointer or grid mode. Compared in detail: [No Mouse Mode vs Homerow](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-homerow) and [Homerow alternatives](https://nomousemode.com/homerow-alternatives).

#### 3. Shortcat: best free search-to-click

[Shortcat](https://shortcat.app) is "the universal command palette for your Mac". Press `⇧⌘Space`, type what you want to click, and it clicks it. After a short delay it also shows letter labels. It handles right, double and modifier clicks, window search, menu search and emoji. It's a free download (the site lists no price), needs macOS 13 or later, and is still a 0.x beta last updated in July 2025. See [No Mouse Mode vs Shortcat](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-shortcat).

#### 4. Wooshy: best for searching the whole screen

[Wooshy](https://wooshy.app) searches the whole macOS interface, including the Dock, the menu bar and the status bar, and clicks what you type. It's a free download that is "full-featured, but takes some random naps"; a subscription of $3.88 a month or $46.28 a year keeps it running all the time. There's no one-time option listed. It needs macOS 14.6 Sonoma, with older builds offered for Ventura and Monterey. It doesn't document a pointer-movement mode.

#### 5. Scoot: best free and open source

[Scoot](https://github.com/mjrusso/scoot) is a "keyboard-driven MacOS cursor actuator" with three modes: element labels (`⇧⌘J`), a grid across all screens (`⇧⌘K`) and freestyle movement using familiar text-editing shortcuts (`⇧⌘L`). It's free, BSD-3-Clause, and maintained (v1.3, March 2026). Its README says it runs on macOS 11 and 12 and doesn't mention newer versions, so check it on yours. Note that its `⇧⌘J` default is the same as No Mouse Mode's scroll areas shortcut.

#### 6. Mouseless: best if you also use Windows or Linux

[Mouseless](https://mouseless.click) promises "lightning-fast mouse control with the keyboard" on macOS, Windows and Linux. Tap Left Command for a grid and type a cell's two characters; tap Left Option for a free mode where I/J/K/L move the pointer. Label mode is in beta. It's closed source and actively maintained (v1.1.0, October 2026). Pricing is "lifetime or subscription", but the amounts aren't published on its site; there's a 14-day trial with no card or email, and each license works on 5 machines.

#### 7. warpd: free, but not updated since 2023

[warpd](https://github.com/rvaiya/warpd) is "a modal keyboard-driven virtual pointer" with hint, grid and normal (hjkl) modes. It's free (MIT), has about 3,660 GitHub stars and also runs on Linux, but its last commit was in June 2023 and the last macOS release was in November 2022. Installing it on a Mac means a prebuilt tarball or a source build. See [warpd for Mac](https://nomousemode.com/warpd-for-mac).

#### 8. Vimac: don't start here today

[Vimac](https://github.com/nchudleigh/vimac), the free open-source app that became Homerow, hasn't been updated since 2022. Its README now says "Vimac is now Homerow". If you liked its hint mode, read [Vimac alternatives](https://nomousemode.com/vimac-alternative).

#### 9. The free macOS built-ins

Before you buy anything, know what your Mac already has:

- **Mouse Keys** (System Settings > Accessibility > Pointer Control) moves the pointer with 7 8 9 U O J K L or the keypad, and clicks with I or keypad 5. It works with no mouse or trackpad at all, which makes it a lifesaver when one breaks. The catch: while it's on you can't type text. More in [No Mouse Mode vs Mouse Keys](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-mouse-keys).
- **Voice Control** (System Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control) lets you say "Show numbers" and "Click" plus a number, or "Show grid" to reach any spot. It's the closest built-in to labels, but you use your voice, not keys.
- **Full Keyboard Access** (System Settings > Accessibility > Motor > Keyboard) highlights the focused control and moves through them with Tab. It works everywhere, but reaching a far-away button can take many presses. See [Full Keyboard Access on Mac](https://nomousemode.com/full-keyboard-access-mac).

#### 10. Vimium: great, but only in the browser

[Vimium](https://github.com/philc/vimium) is a free, actively maintained browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Press `f` and every link in the page gets a hint. If you spend your day in a browser, install it. It can't reach Finder, System Settings, the menu bar, the Dock or other apps, which is where Mac-wide tools come in. More in [Vimium for Mac](https://nomousemode.com/vimium-for-mac).

#### Which one should you choose?

- **Your mouse or trackpad just died:** turn on Mouse Keys now; see [Mac trackpad not working](https://nomousemode.com/mac-trackpad-not-working).
- **You want to click buttons faster and still use a trackpad sometimes:** Homerow, Shortcat or No Mouse Mode's labels.
- **You want to drop the mouse entirely**, for comfort or [RSI](https://nomousemode.com/keyboard-only-mac-rsi): an app that also moves the pointer, drags and scrolls, such as No Mouse Mode, Scoot or Mouseless.
- **You want free and open source:** Scoot.
- **You switch between Mac, Windows and Linux:** Mouseless.
- **You only live in a browser:** Vimium.

New to all this? Start with the hub guide, [how to use a Mac without a mouse](https://nomousemode.com/how-to-use-mac-without-mouse).

**Labels, type to click, a pointer and a grid in one app** No Mouse Mode turns your keyboard into a full mouse for $19.99 one time, with free updates. Price and checkout: https://nomousemode.com/#pricing ($19.99 one-time for 1 Mac, free updates; macOS 14+ on Apple silicon and Intel).

#### FAQ

##### What is the best Vimium-like app for Mac?

Vimium itself only works inside web pages in Chrome, Edge and Firefox. For Vimium-style letter hints in every Mac app, look at [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/), Homerow or Scoot. Vimac was the original free option, but it hasn't been updated since 2022 and its README says it is now Homerow. More in [Vimium for Mac](https://nomousemode.com/vimium-for-mac).

##### Is there a free keyboard mouse app for Mac?

Yes. Scoot is free and open source (BSD-3-Clause) with labels, a grid and a free-moving mode. Shortcat is a free download with no price on its site. warpd is free but not updated since 2023. macOS also has Mouse Keys, Full Keyboard Access and Voice Control built in at no cost.

##### Does macOS have a built-in way to use the mouse with the keyboard?

Yes, Mouse Keys. Turn it on in System Settings > Accessibility > Pointer Control > Mouse Keys, then move with 7 8 9 U O J K L (or the keypad) and click with I or keypad 5. While it's on you can't type text. See [No Mouse Mode vs Mouse Keys](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-mouse-keys).

##### Which mouseless Mac apps have a grid?

No Mouse Mode (a 3×3 grid that zooms in with each press), Scoot, Mouseless and warpd all have a grid mode. Voice Control has one too, but you use it by voice ("Show grid").

##### Is Vimac still maintained?

No. Vimac's last commit was on December 31, 2022, and its README says "Vimac is now Homerow". It still exists as free, open-source code, but if you're starting today, look at a maintained app. See [Vimac alternatives](https://nomousemode.com/vimac-alternative).

##### Which keyboard mouse app works on Mac, Windows and Linux?

Mouseless runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, and each license can be activated on 5 machines. warpd also runs on Linux (X11 and some Wayland setups) and macOS, but it hasn't been updated since 2023.

##### Are you biased?

Yes. This guide is written by the maker of No Mouse Mode. We stick to facts we checked on each app's official site, docs or repository in October 2026, and we say where a free or built-in option is enough.

### Full Keyboard Access on Mac: how to turn it on, the keys, and its limits

Source: https://nomousemode.com/full-keyboard-access-mac  
Updated: 2026-10-31 · Author: Ahmed Gagan (maker of No Mouse Mode)

Your Mac can already be driven from the keyboard. **Turn on Full Keyboard Access, then press Tab to move between controls and Space to press one.** Here's how to set it up, every key Apple documents for it, and where a label-based app gets you there faster.

> **Short answer:** Open **System Settings → Accessibility → Motor → Keyboard** and switch on **Full Keyboard Access**. Then `Tab` moves a highlight to the next item, `Space` selects it, and `Tab`-`H` shows the full list of commands. If you only want Tab to stop on buttons too, press `Control-F7`. It's free and good for settings screens and dialogs. Where it struggles is busy windows: you press Tab over and over to reach one button. A label-based app such as [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) lets you jump straight to it instead.

#### Two built-in settings with similar names

Apple has two separate features here, and they're easy to mix up.

|  | Keyboard navigation | Full Keyboard Access | No Mouse Mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| What it does | Lets Tab stop on every control, not just text boxes and lists | Highlights the focused item and lets you drive the Mac with the keyboard | Moves and clicks the real pointer; labels every clickable thing |
| Where to turn it on | System Settings → Keyboard (Sonoma 14 guide), or Control-F7 | System Settings → Accessibility → Motor → Keyboard | Install the app; it asks for Accessibility permission |
| How you reach a button | Tab, Tab, Tab… | Tab, arrows, Control-Tab | Type its label letters, or part of its name |
| Menu bar and Dock | Control-F2 / Control-F3 | Control-F2 / Control-F3 | Labelled along with the window |
| Price | Free, built in | Free, built in | $19.99 one-time for 1 Mac (as of October 2026), no trial |

If you came here to "tab through buttons", Keyboard navigation (or `Control-F7`) may be all you need. If you want to use the Mac without touching the trackpad at all, Full Keyboard Access is the fuller option.

#### How to turn on Full Keyboard Access

1. Open **System Settings** (Apple menu → System Settings).
2. Choose **Accessibility** in the sidebar.
3. Under **Motor**, choose **Keyboard**.
4. Switch on **Full Keyboard Access**.

That's the path in Apple's current Mac User Guide ([Use Full Keyboard Access](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/use-full-keyboard-access-mchlc06d1059/mac)). On the same screen you can change how the highlight looks: its color, contrast and size. A bigger, higher-contrast highlight makes it much easier to see where you are.

No pointer at all right now? Our [trackpad not working](https://nomousemode.com/mac-trackpad-not-working) guide shows how to get into System Settings using only the keyboard.

#### How to turn on Keyboard navigation (Tab to every button)

Without this, Tab in most windows only jumps between text boxes and lists, and skips buttons and checkboxes. Two ways to change it:

- **The shortcut:** press `Control-F7` (or `Fn-Control-F7` if your top row controls brightness and volume). It switches Tab between all controls and only text boxes and lists.
- **The setting:** in Apple's macOS 14 Sonoma guide, it's System Settings → Keyboard → **Keyboard navigation**. Apple's newer guides no longer have a page for this switch, so if you can't find it, use the shortcut.

With it on, `Tab` goes to the next control and `Shift-Tab` to the previous one.

#### The keys, according to Apple

### Full Keyboard Access

| Press | To |
|---|---|
| Tab / Shift-Tab | Move to the next / previous element |
| Space | Select the focused item |
| Arrow keys | Move within a group |
| Control-Tab / Control-Shift-Tab | Next / previous item |
| Tab-H | Open Commands Help (every command in one list) |
| Control-Option-Command-P | Turn Pass-Through Mode on or off |

##### Focus shortcuts (work alongside either setting)

From Apple's [Mac keyboard shortcuts](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102650) page. Add `Fn` if your function keys control the hardware. Some of these have to be switched on first in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Keyboard.

| Press | Moves focus to |
|---|---|
| Control-F2 | The menu bar. Then arrows to move, Return to open or choose, or type an item's name |
| Control-F3 | The Dock |
| Control-F4 | The active window, or the next one |
| Control-F5 | The window's toolbar |
| Control-F7 | Switches Tab between all controls and only text boxes and lists |
| Control-F8 | The status menus in the menu bar |

#### Where Full Keyboard Access is great

- **Dialogs and settings.** A save sheet or a settings pane has a handful of controls. Tab, Tab, Space, done.
- **Forms.** Tab order on a form usually follows the fields from top to bottom, which is exactly what you want.
- **When there's no pointer at all.** It needs no mouse or trackpad, which makes it a solid fallback when yours stops working.
- **Accessibility needs.** The adjustable highlight and the built-in help make it a dependable everyday tool, and it costs nothing.

#### Its limits

##### You reach things in Tab order, not where your eyes are

Focus moves through a window in the order the app defines. You see the button you want in the top-right corner, but Tab may visit a sidebar, a toolbar and a list before it gets there. In a busy window, that's a lot of presses for one click, and you have to watch the highlight the whole time.

##### It moves focus, not the pointer

Full Keyboard Access selects the focused item. It doesn't put the mouse pointer anywhere. So things that depend on the pointer, such as hovering to reveal a hidden button, dragging, or clicking a spot on a canvas, aren't what it's built for. For those, see [how to move the mouse with the keyboard](https://nomousemode.com/move-mouse-with-keyboard-mac), including Apple's own Mouse Keys.

##### Apps vary

How well Tab works depends on how each app is built. Some apps have a tidy order. Others skip controls or trap focus in one area. That's true of every keyboard tool that relies on what apps tell macOS, ours included.

#### When a label-based app is faster

Instead of walking through controls one by one, a label-based tool shows everything you can click at once. In [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/), press `⇧⌘Space` and every button, link, tab and menu in the front window, plus the menu bar and the Dock, gets a short letter label. Type the label and it's clicked. Other apps use the same idea (see [No Mouse Mode vs Homerow](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-homerow) and [No Mouse Mode vs Shortcat](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-shortcat); Homerow and Shortcat also show ⌘⇧Space in their docs and demos).

A few things No Mouse Mode adds on top of labels:

- **Type to click** (`⇧⌘/`): type part of a button's name, such as "nf" for New Folder, and press Return.
- **Different clicks from a label:** hold Shift for a right-click, Command for a Command-click (a new tab in browsers), Option for a double-click.
- **A real pointer when you need one:** `⇧⌘M` turns on `W` `A` `S` `D` movement, `Space` to click and hold to drag, and a jump grid (`E`) that reaches anywhere in two or three presses, in any app.

The honest trade-off: labels, like Tab, depend on apps describing their buttons to macOS, which most do. For apps that don't, there's an optional setting that reads on-screen text with Apple's on-device text recognition (it needs Screen Recording permission, and nothing is saved or sent), and the grid and W A S D work everywhere. No Mouse Mode costs $19.99 one-time for 1 Mac (as of October 2026) and there's no free trial, but you can try the same keys in the demo on this page. It runs on macOS 14 Sonoma or later, on Apple silicon and Intel.

#### Which should you use?

- **Keyboard navigation (`Control-F7`)** if you mostly type and just want Tab to reach buttons in dialogs.
- **Full Keyboard Access** if you want a free, complete way to run the Mac from the keyboard and don't mind stepping through controls.
- **A label-based app** if you find yourself pressing Tab ten times to reach one button, or you want to click anywhere you can see. Our [guide to using a Mac without a mouse](https://nomousemode.com/how-to-use-mac-without-mouse) puts all the options side by side, and [the best keyboard mouse apps](https://nomousemode.com/best-keyboard-mouse-apps-for-mac) compares the apps.

**Skip the Tab, Tab, Tab** No Mouse Mode puts a short letter label on every button, link and menu, so any of them is one or two keystrokes away. Price and checkout: https://nomousemode.com/#pricing ($19.99 one-time for 1 Mac, free updates; macOS 14+ on Apple silicon and Intel).

#### FAQ

##### How do I turn on Full Keyboard Access on a Mac?

Open System Settings, go to Accessibility, then Motor, then Keyboard, and switch on Full Keyboard Access. That's the path in Apple's current Mac User Guide. Once it's on, the focused item gets a highlight and Tab moves it.

##### What is the difference between Full Keyboard Access and Keyboard navigation?

Keyboard navigation is the simpler setting: when it's on, Tab moves to every control (buttons, checkboxes, pop-up menus), not just text boxes and lists. On macOS 14 Sonoma it's a switch in System Settings → Keyboard, and Control-F7 toggles it. Full Keyboard Access is the bigger accessibility feature: it highlights the focused item, lets you customize that highlight, and adds more keys such as Control-Tab and Tab-H for its Commands Help.

##### How do I tab through buttons on a Mac?

Press Control-F7 (or Fn-Control-F7) to switch Tab between all controls and only text boxes and lists. With all controls on, Tab goes to the next button and Shift-Tab to the previous one. Space presses the focused button when Full Keyboard Access is on.

##### How do I get to the menu bar or Dock without a mouse?

Control-F2 (or Fn-Control-F2) puts focus on the menu bar; use the arrow keys to move, Return to open or choose, or type an item's name. Control-F3 focuses the Dock. Some of these shortcuts must first be turned on in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Keyboard.

##### Why does Control-F7 or Control-F2 do nothing?

On many Mac keyboards the top row controls brightness, volume and so on by default, so add Fn: Fn-Control-F7 or Fn-Control-F2. Apple also says some focus shortcuts have to be enabled first in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Keyboard.

##### Is Full Keyboard Access free?

Yes, it's built into macOS. So are Mouse Keys and Voice Control. If Tab is enough for what you do, you don't need anything else. [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) is a paid app ($19.99 one-time for 1 Mac, as of October 2026, with no free trial) for people who want to click things directly by label.

##### Can I use Full Keyboard Access and No Mouse Mode together?

We haven't documented testing them side by side, so we can't promise how they interact. They do different jobs: Full Keyboard Access moves a focus highlight, while No Mouse Mode moves and clicks the real pointer. No Mouse Mode passes any shortcut that uses Command, Control or Option to the focused app.

### Homerow alternatives for Mac: seven options, honestly compared

Source: https://nomousemode.com/homerow-alternatives  
Updated: 2026-10-31 · Author: Ahmed Gagan (maker of No Mouse Mode)

Homerow is good, but it isn't the only way to click with the keyboard. **No Mouse Mode, Shortcat, Wooshy, Scoot and Mouseless take different approaches, and macOS has free tools built in.**

> **Short answer:** If you want Homerow-style click labels plus a full keyboard mouse, [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) ($19.99 once for one Mac) is the closest match with the most extras. Shortcat and Wooshy are search-first: you type a button's name. Scoot is free and open source, with labels, a grid and a freestyle pointer. Mouseless is grid-first and runs on Mac, Windows and Linux. macOS's built-in tools cost nothing and are enough for light use, and Vimium covers web pages only.

#### Why look past Homerow?

[Homerow](https://www.homerow.app) is a solid, maintained app: it labels buttons so you can click by typing, and it has search and scrolling. As of October 2026 it's $49.99 once for all your personal Macs, needs macOS 13 or later, and is free to try with a reminder every 50 activations. (Our [Homerow vs No Mouse Mode comparison](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-homerow) goes deeper.)

People look for alternatives for a few common reasons: they want to spend less on a single Mac, they want to move the pointer and drag without a mouse too, they want something free or open source, or they need the same tool on Windows or Linux. Each option below answers one of those.

#### Homerow alternatives at a glance

Prices and versions as of October 2026.

| App | Price | Platform | Maintained? | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **No Mouse Mode** | $19.99 once (1 Mac) | macOS 14+, Apple silicon and Intel | Yes, version 2.0.1 | Labels, type to click, WASD pointer, jump grid |
| Shortcat | Free download (no price on site) | macOS 13+ | Last updated July 2025 (0.x beta) | Type to search, then labels |
| Wooshy | Free with naps; $3.88/mo or $46.28/yr | macOS 14.6+ (older builds offered) | Yes | Type to search and click |
| Scoot | Free, open source | macOS (README: 11 and 12) | Yes, v1.3 (March 2026) | Labels, grid, freestyle pointer |
| Mouseless | Not published; 14-day trial | macOS, Windows, Linux | Yes, v1.1.0 (October 2026) | Grid and free movement; labels in beta |
| macOS built-ins | Free | macOS | Part of macOS | Mouse Keys, Full Keyboard Access, Voice Control |
| Vimium | Free, open source | Chrome, Edge, Firefox | Yes | Link hints inside web pages only |

#### 1. No Mouse Mode: labels plus a full keyboard mouse

[No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) is a menu bar app that turns the keyboard into a mouse. Like Homerow, `⇧⌘Space` puts letter labels on every button, link, tab and menu, including the menu bar and the Dock. `⇧⌘/` lets you type part of a button's name instead, and `⇧⌘J` numbers each scrollable pane.

Where it goes further is the pointer. Turn it on with `⇧⌘M` and W A S D move the cursor smoothly (Shift for fast, Q for one-pixel precise), Space clicks or drags, Return right-clicks, and the arrow keys scroll. `E` opens a 3×3 jump grid that reaches any spot in two or three presses, and you can save spots and jump between displays. An optional on-device text recognition mode adds labels in apps that don't describe their buttons to macOS. A Practice window with nine lessons helps you learn it.

**Trade-offs:** no free trial (the site has interactive demos with the same keys instead), all sales are final, and it needs macOS 14 Sonoma or later. It's $19.99 for one Mac, $49.99 for three. For four or more Macs, Homerow's single license costs less.

#### 2. Shortcat: a command palette for clicking

[Shortcat](https://shortcat.app) calls itself "the universal command palette for your Mac". Press `⌘⇧Space`, type what you want to click ("ok" for an OK button), and it clicks. After two seconds (configurable) it also shows yellow labels with one- to three-letter shortcuts. It supports right-clicks, double-clicks and modifier clicks, plus window search, menu search and an emoji mode, and it works in Safari, Chrome, Firefox and most Electron apps.

**Trade-offs:** it's still a 0.x beta, last updated in July 2025, with a beta expiry moved to 2030. Its site doesn't state a price; it's a free download. It has no pointer-movement mode on its feature list. More in [No Mouse Mode vs Shortcat](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-shortcat).

#### 3. Wooshy: search the whole screen

[Wooshy](https://wooshy.app)'s pitch is "Type. Return. Done." It searches the whole macOS interface, including the Dock, the menu bar and the status icons on the right, and clicks what you pick. It's a search-to-click tool; it doesn't document a pointer-movement mode.

**Trade-offs:** the free version is "full-featured, but takes some random naps". To keep it running all the time you subscribe for $3.88 a month or $46.28 a year; there's no one-time option listed. It needs macOS 14.6, though older builds are offered for Ventura and Monterey.

#### 4. Scoot: free, open source, three modes

[Scoot](https://github.com/mjrusso/scoot) is a "keyboard-driven MacOS cursor actuator" that can move, click, drag and scroll. It has three modes: `⇧⌘J` shows labels on buttons and links in the focused window, `⇧⌘K` shows a grid of equal cells across your screens, and `⇧⌘L` lets you nudge the cursor with familiar text-editing shortcuts. All shortcuts can be changed, and it installs with `brew install --cask scoot`.

**Trade-offs:** its README only says it runs on macOS 11 and 12, so check it on your version. It's free (BSD-3-Clause), has about 535 GitHub stars as of October 2026, and was updated in March 2026.

#### 5. Mouseless: grid-first, on every desktop

[Mouseless](https://mouseless.click) offers "lightning-fast mouse control with the keyboard" on macOS, Windows and Linux. Tap Left Command to show a grid, type a cell's two characters, then press Space to click its center or a sub-key for a finer spot. Tap Left Option for free mode, where I J K L move the pointer. Label mode, Homerow's main feature, is still in beta.

**Trade-offs:** its site offers "lifetime or subscription" but doesn't publish prices. There's a 14-day trial with no card or email, each license works on 5 machines, and there's a 25% academic discount. It was updated in October 2026.

#### 6. macOS built-ins: free and already installed

Before buying anything, see whether Apple's tools are enough:

- **Mouse Keys** (System Settings > Accessibility > Pointer Control) moves the pointer with keys like 7 8 9 U O J K L and clicks with I. Apple notes that while it's on, you can't use the keyboard to type text. See [No Mouse Mode vs Mouse Keys](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-mouse-keys).
- **Full Keyboard Access** (Accessibility > Motor > Keyboard) lets you Tab through controls and press Space to select. Our [Full Keyboard Access guide](https://nomousemode.com/full-keyboard-access-mac) covers it.
- **Voice Control** can label items: say "Show numbers", then "Click" and the number. It also has a numbered grid.

These are free and dependable. They're slower than click labels for everyday use, but for occasional use or a [trackpad that has stopped working](https://nomousemode.com/mac-trackpad-not-working), they may be all you need.

#### 7. Vimium: link hints, but only in the browser

[Vimium](https://github.com/philc/vimium) is a free, open-source browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Press `f` and every link on the page gets a hint; type it to follow the link (`F` opens it in a new tab). It's actively maintained and excellent at what it does.

**Trade-offs:** it only works inside web pages. It can't reach Finder, System Settings, the menu bar, the Dock or other apps, and Safari isn't on its list. If you love Vimium and want the same idea everywhere, read [Vimium for the whole Mac](https://nomousemode.com/vimium-for-mac).

#### How to choose

- **You want to leave the mouse behind entirely:** [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/), for labels, pointer movement, dragging and a grid in one app.
- **You'd rather type names than letters:** Shortcat or Wooshy. No Mouse Mode's type to click does this too.
- **You want free and open source:** Scoot.
- **You switch between Mac, Windows and Linux:** Mouseless.
- **You only need it now and then:** the macOS built-ins.
- **You only care about the web:** Vimium.
- **You're happy with labels and use many Macs:** Homerow itself is still a fine choice.

For a broader look, see the [best keyboard mouse apps for Mac](https://nomousemode.com/best-keyboard-mouse-apps-for-mac), or start with [how to use a Mac without a mouse](https://nomousemode.com/how-to-use-mac-without-mouse).

**Labels, a jump grid and a keyboard mouse in one app** No Mouse Mode is $19.99 once for one Mac, with free updates and no subscription. Price and checkout: https://nomousemode.com/#pricing ($19.99 one-time for 1 Mac, free updates; macOS 14+ on Apple silicon and Intel).

#### FAQ

##### What is the best Homerow alternative?

It depends on what you want. For labels plus a full keyboard mouse (W A S D movement, every mouse button, a jump grid), try [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/). For typing a button's name, look at Shortcat or Wooshy. For something free and open source, Scoot. For one tool across Mac, Windows and Linux, Mouseless.

##### Is there a free alternative to Homerow?

Yes. Scoot is free and open source (BSD-3-Clause). Shortcat is a free download, though its site doesn't state a price. Wooshy has a free version that "takes some random naps". macOS itself includes Mouse Keys, Full Keyboard Access and Voice Control at no cost.

##### Is there a Homerow alternative for Windows or Linux?

Mouseless runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, and each license can be activated on 5 machines. The other apps on this page are Mac only, apart from Vimium, which runs inside Chrome, Edge and Firefox on any system.

##### Is Shortcat still maintained?

Shortcat was last updated in July 2025 (v0.12.2), and it's still a 0.x beta. Version 0.12.1 moved its beta expiry to 2030, so it keeps working for now.

##### What happened to Vimac?

Vimac became Homerow. The free open-source Vimac hasn't been updated since 2022. See [Vimac alternatives](https://nomousemode.com/vimac-alternative) for what to use today.

##### Does any alternative have a free trial?

Homerow itself is free to try, with a reminder every 50 activations. Mouseless has a 14-day trial with no card or email. No Mouse Mode has no free trial; its website has interactive demos that use the same keys instead.

### How to use a Mac without a mouse or trackpad

Source: https://nomousemode.com/how-to-use-mac-without-mouse  
Updated: 2026-10-31 · Author: Ahmed Gagan (maker of No Mouse Mode)

You can run a Mac from the keyboard alone. **macOS has Full Keyboard Access, Mouse Keys and Voice Control built in, and an app like No Mouse Mode lets you click any button by typing its label.** Here's every method, what it's good at, and how to set one up in five minutes.

> **Short answer:** Start with what's built in: **Full Keyboard Access** (Tab between controls, Space to press) plus **Control-F2** for the menu bar and **Control-F3** for the Dock. That covers a lot of everyday work. Where it falls short is anything that needs a pointer: a web page, a canvas, a right-click, a drag. **Mouse Keys** fills that gap for free but blocks typing while it's on. If you want to click any button in a couple of keystrokes and steer the pointer smoothly, an app like [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) does both.

#### Why go mouse-free?

People land here for different reasons. The trackpad or mouse just died and you need to get through the day. Your wrist hurts after long sessions. Or you already live on the keyboard in a code editor and reaching for the trackpad breaks your flow. The good news: macOS was built with keyboard users in mind, and the gaps it leaves are easy to fill.

If your trackpad has stopped working right now, jump to [what to do when your Mac trackpad isn't working](https://nomousemode.com/mac-trackpad-not-working). If it's about comfort, see [using a Mac keyboard-only for wrist pain](https://nomousemode.com/keyboard-only-mac-rsi).

#### Built in: Full Keyboard Access and keyboard navigation

Full Keyboard Access highlights the item that has focus and lets you move around with the keyboard instead of a pointer. You can change the highlight's color, contrast and size, which helps a lot on a busy screen.

1. Open System Settings → **Accessibility → Motor → Keyboard**.
2. Switch on **Full Keyboard Access**.

The keys:

- `Tab` / `⇧Tab`: next or previous element.
- `Space`: select or press the focused item.
- Arrow keys: move within a group.
- `⌃Tab` / `⌃⇧Tab`: next or previous item.
- `Tab`-`H`: opens Commands Help, a list of everything else.
- `⌃⌥⌘P`: Pass-Through Mode, for apps that need those keys themselves.

On macOS 14 Sonoma there's also a lighter setting called **Keyboard navigation** in System Settings → Keyboard. With it on, Tab moves to every control; with it off, Tab only moves between text boxes and lists. `⌃F7` flips between the two. Our [Full Keyboard Access guide](https://nomousemode.com/full-keyboard-access-mac) goes deeper.

The catch: Tab visits controls one at a time, in order. Reaching the twentieth button in a toolbar means a lot of presses, and many web pages and custom-drawn apps don't play nicely with it.

#### Built in: the focus shortcuts

These jump straight to parts of the screen that Tab can't easily reach. Some need switching on first in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Keyboard. On some keyboards you add Fn (for example Fn-Control-F2).

| Shortcut | Moves focus to |
|---|---|
| ⌃F2 | The menu bar. Use the arrows to move, Return to open or choose, or type an item's name. |
| ⌃F3 | The Dock |
| ⌃F4 | The active window or the next one |
| ⌃F5 | The window's toolbar |
| ⌃F8 | The status menus on the right of the menu bar |

#### Built in: Mouse Keys

Mouse Keys turns part of your keyboard into a pointer. Turn it on in System Settings → **Accessibility → Pointer Control → Mouse Keys**, or press `⌥⌘F5` to open the Accessibility Shortcuts panel. Then:

- **Move:** `7` `8` `9` `U` `O` `J` `K` `L` (or the numeric keypad).
- **Click:** `I` (keypad 5).
- **Press and hold:** `M` (keypad 0); **release:** `.`

It works with no pointer device at all, and it's free. The big limit, in Apple's words: "When Mouse Keys is on, you can't use the keyboard or numeric keypad to enter text." So you toggle it constantly. One of its options lets you press Option five times to do that. We compare it head to head in [No Mouse Mode vs Mouse Keys](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-mouse-keys), and cover the details in [how to move the mouse with the keyboard](https://nomousemode.com/move-mouse-with-keyboard-mac).

#### Built in: Voice Control

If you'd rather talk than type, turn on System Settings → Accessibility → **Voice Control**. Say "Show numbers" (or "Show names") and on-screen items get labels; say "Click" and the number to press one. "Show grid" puts a numbered grid over the screen, "Show window grid" limits it to the front window, and saying a grid number zooms in. "Hide numbers", "Hide grid" and "Stop listening" put it away.

It's powerful and free, but speaking every click is slow for a full workday and awkward in a shared office.

#### What about Control-click?

Apple calls a right-click a "secondary click or Control-click": hold `Control` while you click. That still needs a working mouse or trackpad. For keyboard-only ways, including the Contextual Menu key on some Apple keyboards, see [how to right-click without a mouse](https://nomousemode.com/right-click-without-mouse-mac).

#### No Mouse Mode: click anything, steer when you need to

[No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) is a menu bar app that fills the gaps above. It gives you two ways to work, and you can mix them.

##### Click labels (`⇧⌘Space`)

Every button, link, tab, menu, the menu bar and the Dock get a short letter label. Type the letters and it's clicked. Hold `⇧` with the last letter to right-click, `⌘` to Command-click (a new tab in browsers), `⌥` to double-click, or `⌃` to just move the pointer there. Tab keeps labels coming back for several clicks in a row, and labels for a window stay the same each time, so your fingers learn them.

##### Type to click (`⇧⌘/`)

Type part of what a button says, and press Return. Case, spaces and accents don't matter, and initials work: "nf" finds New Folder.

##### Scroll areas (`⇧⌘J`)

Every scrollable pane gets a number. Pick one, then scroll with J/K or the arrows, page with Space, and jump to the top or bottom with T and B.

##### W A S D pointer mode (`⇧⌘M`)

For things that aren't buttons, like a spot in a photo or a slider, turn No Mouse Mode on. `W` `A` `S` `D` move the pointer smoothly and it eases in; hold Shift to go fast or Q for one-pixel precision. `Space` clicks (twice to double-click, hold to drag), `Return` right-clicks, `M` middle-clicks, and the arrow keys scroll. Click into a text box and it turns itself off so you can type.

##### Jump grid (`E`)

A 3×3 grid labelled Q W E / A S D / Z X C covers the screen and zooms in with each press, so two or three keys reach any point. It works in every app, even ones that don't describe their buttons to macOS.

Honest trade-off: labels depend on apps telling macOS where their buttons are. Most do. For ones that don't, you can turn on optional on-screen text reading (Apple's on-device text recognition, needs Screen Recording; nothing is saved or sent), or use the grid and W A S D, which work everywhere.

#### Every method compared

|  | Full Keyboard Access | Mouse Keys | Voice Control | No Mouse Mode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Price | Free, built in | Free, built in | Free, built in | $19.99 one time, 1 Mac (as of October 2026) |
| Click a specific button | Tab to it, then Space | Steer the pointer there | Say its number or name | Type its label or name |
| Move the pointer | No | Yes, number keys | Grid by voice | Yes, W A S D plus grid |
| Right-click | Control-click needs a pointer | Needs Alternate pointer actions | Yes, by voice | Yes, Return or ⇧ + label |
| Scroll a chosen pane | n/a | n/a | n/a | Yes, scroll areas |
| Type while it's on | Yes | No | Dictation | Label shortcuts work any time; pointer mode turns off in text boxes |
| Works with no pointer device | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

Other apps do parts of this too. [Homerow](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-homerow) ($49.99 one time as of October 2026) and [Shortcat](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-shortcat) focus on clicking by label or search. Vimac, the free open-source app that became Homerow, hasn't been updated since 2022 (see [Vimac alternatives](https://nomousemode.com/vimac-alternative)). The roundup is in [the best keyboard mouse apps for Mac](https://nomousemode.com/best-keyboard-mouse-apps-for-mac) and [Homerow alternatives](https://nomousemode.com/homerow-alternatives).

Coming from another tool? We've written guides for [Vimium users](https://nomousemode.com/vimium-for-mac) (browser link hints only reach the web page, not Finder or the Dock), [keynav](https://nomousemode.com/keynav-for-mac) (X11 only, no macOS) and [warpd](https://nomousemode.com/warpd-for-mac) (not updated since 2023).

#### Set up a mouse-free Mac in 5 minutes

1. **Turn on Full Keyboard Access** in System Settings → Accessibility → Motor → Keyboard. Tab and Space now reach most controls.
2. **Learn `⌃F2` and `⌃F3`** for the menu bar and Dock. If they do nothing, switch them on in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Keyboard.
3. **Add a way to click anything.** [Download No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/download), drag it to Applications and open it. The guided setup walks you through Accessibility permission and your license key.
4. **Click by label.** Press `⇧⌘Space` and type the letters on whatever you want to click.
5. **Steer when you need to.** Press `⇧⌘M`, move with W A S D, click with Space, right-click with Return, and press E for the grid.
6. **Practise.** Open the Practice window from the menu bar icon for nine short hands-on lessons. Press H whenever you forget a key.

Stuck on a step? The [support page](https://nomousemode.com/support) covers permissions, licenses and every key.

#### Tips that make keyboard-only stick

The first day is the hardest. A few habits help:

- **Click by label first, steer second.** Most clicks are on buttons, links and menus. Labels or type to click get you there in two or three keys; save W A S D and the grid for everything else.
- **Let it switch itself off.** No Mouse Mode turns itself off when you click into a text box, and you can list apps where it always stays off, such as a game or a code editor with its own keys.
- **Try hold-to-use.** If a toggle feels like one more thing to remember, set it to work only while you hold Right Command or Right Option.
- **Save your common spots.** Press `⇧` and a number over a spot you hit all the time, then the number alone jumps back there.
- **Keep the built-ins.** `⌃F2` for the menu bar and `⌘Space` for Spotlight still work alongside everything else.

On privacy: No Mouse Mode never stores or sends your keystrokes. It only goes online to activate and re-check your license and to check for updates.

#### Which should you use?

- **Trackpad broken for a day:** Full Keyboard Access and Mouse Keys will get you through, for free.
- **You'd rather speak:** Voice Control.
- **Keyboard-only all day, in every app:** built-ins plus an app that clicks by label and steers the pointer. That's the job [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) was built for. See [pricing](https://nomousemode.com/#pricing).

#### FAQ

##### Can you use a Mac with only a keyboard?

Yes. Turn on Full Keyboard Access in System Settings → Accessibility → Motor → Keyboard to move between controls with Tab and press them with Space. Control-F2 reaches the menu bar and Control-F3 the Dock. For anything that needs a pointer, Mouse Keys moves it with the number keys, or an app like [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) lets you click buttons by typing their labels.

##### How do I control the mouse with the keyboard on a Mac?

Turn on Mouse Keys in System Settings → Accessibility → Pointer Control. Then 7 8 9 U O J K L move the pointer and I clicks. You can't type text while it's on. [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) uses W A S D instead, with smooth movement, a fast and a precise mode, and Space to click. See [how to move the mouse with the keyboard](https://nomousemode.com/move-mouse-with-keyboard-mac).

##### How do I right-click without a mouse on a Mac?

With a working trackpad, hold Control and click. Keyboard only, macOS offers Alternate pointer actions or Voice Control. In [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/), Return right-clicks where the pointer is, and holding Shift while you type a label's last letter right-clicks that button. The full list is in [how to right-click without a mouse](https://nomousemode.com/right-click-without-mouse-mac).

##### My trackpad stopped working. How do I turn on Bluetooth without it?

Apple's tip: press Command-Space, type Bluetooth File Exchange, press Return, then press Return again to turn Bluetooth on. More fixes are in [what to do when your Mac trackpad isn't working](https://nomousemode.com/mac-trackpad-not-working).

##### Is there a free way to click buttons by keyboard on a Mac?

Yes. Full Keyboard Access is built in and free, and Voice Control's "Show numbers" labels on-screen items for you to click by voice. Free open-source apps exist too, such as Scoot. [The best keyboard mouse apps for Mac](https://nomousemode.com/best-keyboard-mouse-apps-for-mac) compares them with paid ones.

##### Does No Mouse Mode have a free trial?

No. It's $19.99 one time for 1 Mac, with free updates and no subscription. The [website](https://nomousemode.com/) has interactive demos that use the same keys, so you can try how it feels before you [buy](https://nomousemode.com/#pricing).

##### Which macOS versions does No Mouse Mode work on?

macOS 14 Sonoma or later, including Sequoia and Tahoe, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

### A keyboard-only Mac workflow: how to reach for the mouse less

Source: https://nomousemode.com/keyboard-only-mac-rsi  
Updated: 2026-10-31 · Author: Ahmed Gagan (maker of No Mouse Mode)

If your wrist or hand hurts, **see a doctor or physiotherapist first**. If you've decided you want to use the mouse or trackpad less, here's how to do it on a Mac, with free built-ins, a few shortcuts and click labels, adopted gradually over one week.

> **Short answer:** **This isn't medical advice.** If you have pain, numbness or tingling, see a doctor or physiotherapist. If you want to use the mouse or trackpad less, a Mac can do a lot from the keyboard: `⌘Space` to open apps, Full Keyboard Access and Voice Control built in, and the shortcuts in every app's menus. For clicking things you can see, a label app like [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) lets you press `⇧⌘Space` and type a button's letters. Change one habit at a time; the one-week plan below shows how.

#### First: what this page is and isn't

We make a keyboard app, not medical advice. We won't tell you what causes wrist pain, whether a keyboard is better for you than a mouse, or what will make it go away, because we don't know your situation and it isn't our field. A doctor or physiotherapist can look at how you work, including your keyboard, chair, desk and breaks, and tell you what to change.

What we can do is explain, practically, how to run a Mac with less reaching for the pointer, if that's part of the plan you've settled on. Use as much or as little of it as you like.

#### Where mouse and trackpad use comes from

Notice what you reach for the pointer to do. For most people it's a short list:

- opening and switching apps;
- pressing buttons, links, tabs and menu items;
- scrolling;
- right-clicking for a menu;
- dragging, selecting, and clicking a spot that isn't a button.

Each one has a keyboard answer. You don't have to replace all of them on day one.

#### Free things built into your Mac

| Built-in | Good for | Turn on |
|---|---|---|
| **Spotlight** (⌘Space) | Opening apps and files by name | Already on |
| **Full Keyboard Access** | Tabbing through buttons in dialogs and settings; Space to press | System Settings → Accessibility → Motor → Keyboard |
| **Focus shortcuts** | Control-F2 menu bar, Control-F3 Dock, Control-F7 Tab to all controls | Some need switching on in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Keyboard |
| **Voice Control** | "Show numbers", then "Click" and a number; "Show grid" for anywhere | System Settings → Accessibility → Voice Control |
| **Mouse Keys** | Moving the pointer with 7 8 9 U O J K L, I to click | System Settings → Accessibility → Pointer Control → Mouse Keys, or ⌥⌘F5 |

All of these are free and may be enough. Their trade-offs: Full Keyboard Access visits controls in Tab order, so a busy window can take many presses (see [our Full Keyboard Access guide](https://nomousemode.com/full-keyboard-access-mac)). Mouse Keys stops you typing text while it's on, and Apple's Mouse Keys page has no right-click key ([No Mouse Mode vs Mouse Keys](https://nomousemode.com/no-mouse-mode-vs-mouse-keys) covers this). Voice Control means speaking out loud, which suits some places better than others.

#### Keyboard shortcuts: the easiest wins

Mac apps show keyboard shortcuts next to their menu items. Open a menu with `Control-F2` (or `Fn-Control-F2`), look along the right-hand side, and pick the two or three you use most. Learning a shortcut for something you do twenty times a day is the cheapest change you can make, and it costs nothing to try.

If you use a keyboard app, check that it doesn't get in the way of these. In No Mouse Mode, any shortcut with Command, Control or Option (like `⌘S`, `⌘W` or `Control-→`) goes straight to your app, even while No Mouse Mode is on.

#### Clicking what you can see: No Mouse Mode

Shortcuts don't cover the button in the middle of a web page or the file in a Finder window. That's the gap [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) fills. It's one of several apps that do this (see [the best keyboard mouse apps for Mac](https://nomousemode.com/best-keyboard-mouse-apps-for-mac)), so compare before you buy.

##### Click labels

Press `⇧⌘Space`. Every button, link, tab and menu in the front window, plus the menu bar and the Dock, gets a short letter label. Type it to click. Hold `Shift` with the last letter to right-click, `Command` for a Command-click (a new tab in browsers), or `Option` to double-click. `Tab` keeps the labels open for several clicks in a row. Labels for a window stay the same each time, so frequent clicks turn into muscle memory.

##### Type to click

Press `⇧⌘/` and type part of what a button says: case, spaces and accents don't matter, and first letters work ("nf" finds New Folder). `Return` clicks. Handy when you know the name but don't want to look for a label.

##### Hold-to-use with Right Command

If switching modes feels like one more thing to remember, turn on hold-to-use in Settings and choose **Right Command** (or Right Option). Hold it, use the mouse keys, let go and you're typing again. It's off by default; `⇧⌘M` works either way.

##### Moving the pointer, scrolling and dragging

While it's on, `W` `A` `S` `D` move the pointer smoothly (hold `Shift` for fast, `Q` for one-pixel precise), `Space` clicks and held down drags, `Return` right-clicks, and the arrow keys scroll. `⇧⌘J` numbers each scrollable pane so you can pick one and page through it. The jump grid (`E`) reaches anywhere on screen in two or three presses, in any app.

##### Saved spots

If you click the same place again and again, such as a send button or a toolbar in an app without labels, hold `Shift` and press `1`–`9` to save the pointer's position. Press the number to jump back there, and ``` to return to where you were before the jump.

##### Practice

The first-run setup walks you through it, and the Practice window (in the menu bar icon) has nine hands-on lessons. Press `H` any time it's on to see every key. Every key and shortcut can be changed in Settings.

Honest limits: labels and type to click depend on apps describing their buttons to macOS, which most do. For apps that don't, an optional setting reads on-screen text with Apple's on-device text recognition (needs Screen Recording permission; nothing is saved or sent), and the grid and W A S D work everywhere. No Mouse Mode costs $19.99 one-time for 1 Mac (as of October 2026), with no free trial; the demo on this page uses the same keys. It runs on macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon and Intel.

#### A gradual one-week plan

Going cold turkey tends to be frustrating. Keep the trackpad or mouse within reach all week and use it whenever you're stuck. The goal is to move one kind of task at a time. If anything is uncomfortable, stop and talk to your doctor or physio.

1. **Day 1: Open apps from the keyboard.** Use `⌘Space` and type the app's name. Don't change anything else.
2. **Day 2: Three shortcuts.** Pick the three menu commands you use most and learn their shortcuts from the menus.
3. **Day 3: Click buttons without the pointer.** Try click labels (`⇧⌘Space`) or Full Keyboard Access in one app you use a lot. If you have No Mouse Mode, run through a few Practice lessons first.
4. **Day 4: Scroll and right-click.** Use the arrow keys to scroll and `Return` (or Shift with a label) to right-click. Try scroll areas (`⇧⌘J`) on a long page.
5. **Day 5: Type to click and hold-to-use.** Try `⇧⌘/` for buttons you know by name. Turn on hold-to-use with Right Command if toggling feels clumsy.
6. **Day 6: Your awkward spots.** Save a spot (`Shift`+number) for anything you click often that has no label, and use the jump grid (`E`) for the rest.
7. **Day 7: Review.** Note which tasks still send your hand to the trackpad. Keep what helped, drop what didn't, and change any key that feels awkward in Settings.

- [How to move the mouse with the keyboard](https://nomousemode.com/move-mouse-with-keyboard-mac): Mouse Keys and the app alternatives.
- [How to right-click without a mouse](https://nomousemode.com/right-click-without-mouse-mac).
- [Support](https://nomousemode.com/support): setup, permissions and every key.

And once more, because it matters: if it hurts, get it looked at by a professional. A tool can change how you work; it can't diagnose why something hurts.

Price and checkout: https://nomousemode.com/#pricing ($19.99 one-time for 1 Mac, free updates; macOS 14+ on Apple silicon and Intel).

#### FAQ

##### Will using the keyboard instead of a mouse help my RSI?

We can't tell you that, and this page isn't medical advice. Pain, numbness or tingling in your hands or wrists is something to take to a doctor or physiotherapist, who can look at your situation, including how you use the keyboard. This guide only covers the practical side: how to use a Mac with less mouse and trackpad if that's what you've decided to do.

##### Can you use a Mac entirely without a mouse or trackpad?

Yes, for most everyday work. macOS has Full Keyboard Access, Mouse Keys and Voice Control built in, and keyboard shortcuts cover a lot. Apps like [No Mouse Mode](https://nomousemode.com/) add click labels and keyboard pointer movement that work across apps. Some apps don't describe their buttons to macOS, so label-based tools fall back to a grid or moving the pointer in those.

##### What's the quickest way to start a mouseless workflow on Mac?

Pick one habit at a time. Start with opening apps from the keyboard and the shortcuts you already half-know, then add one way of clicking buttons (Full Keyboard Access, Voice Control or click labels). The one-week plan on this page breaks it into small daily steps.

##### Is there a way to use No Mouse Mode only while holding a key?

Yes. In Settings, turn on hold-to-use and pick Right Command or Right Option. Hold the key to use the mouse keys, let go to go back to typing. It's off by default, and ⇧⌘M still toggles it either way.

##### Can I use voice instead of the keyboard?

macOS Voice Control lets you click by speaking: say "Show numbers" and then "Click" with a number, or "Show grid" to click anywhere. Turn it on in System Settings → Accessibility → Voice Control. Whether voice, keyboard or a mix suits you best is a good question for your doctor or physio.

##### How long does it take to get used to working without a mouse?

It varies from person to person, and we haven't measured it. Going gradually helps: keep the trackpad within reach for the first days and only switch one task at a time. No Mouse Mode includes a Practice window with nine short lessons, and pressing H shows every key.

##### How much does No Mouse Mode cost?

$19.99 one-time for 1 Mac (as of October 2026), with free updates and no subscription. There's no free trial, but the demo on this page uses the same keys. It runs on macOS 14 Sonoma or later, on Apple silicon and Intel. See [pricing](https://nomousemode.com/#pricing).
